answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce tokens in a vault before it may vote on reputation. Influence is capped by total stake, not account count, so splitting one deposit across many sybils adds no weight. A terrace of independent reviewers can verify fraud and slash the bond. The attacker must acquire or immobilize real capital, risk losing it, and pay more to gain influence. The token lock is a signal of costly commitment, not proof that an identity is unique.
